# r122 — actual file decoder and a retained cleanup defect

**INCOMPLETE_STOP — demonstrated product cleanup failure.** Chromium received one malformed base64 data string through the actual file `index.html` asset-chunk transport with valid envelope fields. Native worker `atob` failed; the host became unavailable with current initial-v5 content, terminated the failed worker and cleared pending ownership. One retry with original chunks reached current admitted final refinement.

The run also reported the unexpected page error **`window.SalahMoonAssetChunk is not a function`**. This prevents qualification despite the recovered final image. [Independent review](../reviews/file-atob-r122-result-review-r1.json) confirms a source-supported cleanup race: `moon/src/moon-native.mjs` removes the script and deletes the global chunk callback in `closeWorker()`, while `tools/build_moon.py` emits an unconditional callback invocation in each asynchronous chunk script. Removing a pending script does not establish cancellation of its execution. The fault observer changes only one worker-message payload; it does not delete the callback. The report does not preserve the exact offending script URL/stack/time, so none is asserted.

Firefox was not launched after this affected path stopped. No repeat or additional source correction was made. The coordinated r119 source-correction pass was already complete; the finite owner order requires retaining this remaining product defect as a blocker while completing independent unaffected rows. This case does not cover `offline.html` or native image decoding.
